description: Vamos a ganar, si quieres ganar únete.
summary:
The app accompanies the crew member from training on the ground to operations in orbit. A longitudinal analysis engine processes trends over time, calibrates each individual's baseline and crosses physical biometrics with cognitive load to flag operational risks before they can affect the mission. AI medical assistants for astronauts already exist, such as NASA and Google's CMO-DA, so Ergosphere Co. sets itself apart in three ways: an individual baseline built from training, the crossing with cognitive load as the mission is accompanied, and attention to diverse profiles. The system supports the tools given to the crew and strengthens research on Earth and human decision-making; the app does not diagnose or treat on its own.

Ships chart routes between the stars; we chart the invisible map of those who fly them.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Ergosphere Co is a web app that follows each astronaut from training on the ground to the way home. It has two sides. The crew member reports what only they know: how they slept, short validated mental-health check-ins (PHQ, GAD, PSS-4, UCLA-3), medications taken, exercise sessions, and a request to talk to someone. The ground medical team sees every reading in Mission Control, with what needs attention first.

HOW IT WORKS

Each crew member is compared with themselves, never with an average. The app builds a personal baseline from the readings logged during training, compares today with their own last two weeks, fits the week's trend and carries it forward seven days. It sets body readings (sleep, heart rate, mood) beside reaction time in a short decompression game and the check-ins, so a physical change and a cognitive one can be read together. In an emergency, a crew code opens a crewmate's data in seconds, as in CPR, and an SOS asks who is needed first.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Flight surgeons get an early signal before a problem affects the mission, and crews on longer missions, with delayed contact, get a tool that works offline on any phone. The app supports the people who decide: it contains no AI, and it does not diagnose or prescribe.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript (ES modules, no frameworks or dependencies), 429 automated tests with Node's test runner, Vercel hosting with one serverless function, Upstash Redis for device sync, Web Crypto (data is encrypted on the device before it leaves it), WebAuthn for fingerprint sign-in. NASA sources: NASA-STD-3001 limits, Human Research Program risks, OCHMO technical briefs, the NASA Life Sciences Portal, RadLab ISS radiation data and DONKI space weather. AI tools were used to write code, tests and text; their use is logged in the repository.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

Earlier work such as NASA and Google's CMO-DA proof of concept explores AI assistants for diagnosis. Ergosphere takes a different path: a baseline built before launch, body and mind read side by side, and care that continues after landing. It is in English and Spanish, with profiles each crew member can make their own. We focused on the mind as much as the body: mental health and neurodivergence are discussed far more openly today than before, and one member of our team is neurodivergent, which shaped how the app asks and listens, our team's pharmaceutical chemist reviewed the ten medications in the onboard kit and shaped how the app follows each dose: when to ask "Did it work?", how long a medication counts before a critical task, and when to stop or watch for side effects. Her values appear as "pharmacist review", never as NASA's words. The app records and follows up; it never prescribes.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Every health fact shown is quoted word for word from its source and checked by a test; values without a source are labelled as app rules. Crew data in the demo is fictional and marked as simulated. A crew member does not see their own readings unless an emergency opens them, and the ground sees every opening. Medication content was reviewed by the team's pharmaceutical chemist.
